questions.stem: How many completely separated individual chambers does a normal, healthy human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two upper chambers called the left and right atria, and two lower chambers called the left and right ventricles. This prevents the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

questions.stem: Which specific major blood vessel is unique because it carries oxygen-rich (oxygenated) blood directly from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart?
questions.explanation: Generally, veins carry deoxygenated blood and arteries carry oxygenated blood. However, the pulmonary vein is the exception—it carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

questions.stem: The natural biological 'pacemaker' of the human heart, responsible for initiating and maintaining the rhythmic heartbeat, is scientifically known as the:
questions.explanation: The Sinoatrial (SA) Node is a specialized bundle of neurons located in the upper wall of the right atrium. It generates electrical impulses automatically, setting the pace of the heart rate.

questions.stem: Which specific anatomical valve strictly prevents the backward flow of deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle back into the right atrium?
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve is situated between the right atrium and the right ventricle. It allows blood to flow only one way. The bicuspid (or mitral) valve does the same job on the left side of the heart.
